result.title: StopLoss: Teaching Agents to Predict Failure and Stop Early
result.summary: Coding agents keep working on runs that will fail verification, and asking a frontier model to watch for this is expensive in its own right. We introduce StopLoss, a small external monitor that learns failure recognition from completed trajectories and their verifier outcomes. The name is inspired by the stop-loss order in finance: StopLoss ends a run early when the run is likely to fail, which saves resources. Final outcomes label earlier local windows, so a fine-tuned language model can score the most recent tool steps in a single forward pass, and a threshold calibrated on successful runs turns that score into an abort decision without changing the executor. Trained on GPT-family SWE-rebench trajectories and evaluated on SWE-bench Verified and a SWE-bench Pro subset with GPT and Claude executors, StopLoss is compared against six general-purpose judges reading identical windows. Outcome supervision lifts failure prediction from near chance to a useful signal at the first check, at one to two orders of magnitude lower cost per check than any tested judge. This translates into savings: relative to completing every task, StopLoss lowers cost per retained solve by 4.5\% on Verified while preserving 99\% of successful runs, and by up to 31\% on the costlier Pro subset, reaching 48\% with a Qwen3-8B backbone, and in all four settings its cost per retained solve is below that of every judge policy. Outcome-trained small monitors can make failure recognition cheap enough for early stopping to pay for itself.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 StopLoss，一个小型外部监控器，从完成的 coding agent 轨迹及其验证结果中学习失败识别，单次前向即可为最近若干工具步骤打分，并用成功轨迹校准的阈值决定是否提前中止运行，以节省算力。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「以最终结果监督早期窗口、再以校准阈值触发提前停止」的机制，可能为 LVR 的 STOP 决策、停止时机与计算成本权衡提供可核查线索；但对象为纯文本 coding agent，未涉及视觉内部状态，迁移到多模态 latent 推理需进一步判断。
